messages.text: My nerdoctaxe 3.1 just stopped hashing.  Fans still power on but screen is dead and no hashing.
Used route to tech
Understood.
Used the store-orders skill

Back with you on the order side, Todd.

Shop···· matches: NerdOctaxe (12TH/s), delivered July 10. That's the unit, so Hal's findings are attached to the right order.

Hal confirmed it as a board-level fault, and the return is with JD and Georges for approval now. They're reviewing it and will confirm shortly, here or by email.

Nothing for you to do yet, please don't ship anything back until the approval and the prepaid label come through. One question: was the unit ever overclocked?
Yes, it was overclocked, I'm guessing but i believe it was at 650 and 1170
Handed to the team · Overclocked unit, warranty coverage is JD's or Georges' decision, not mine.

Thanks for being straight with me about that.

I have to say it plainly: overclocked or modified units fall outside warranty cover, so that changes the picture on this one. Whether an exception is made here is JD's and Georges' call, not mine, and I've put the overclock detail in front of them with Hal's findings.

They'll come back on it shortly. Stay in the chat if you can, and if you step away the answer reaches you by email.
do you still want video

Yes, please send both if you can: a short clip from plug-in through the first 30 seconds, and a clear photo of the serial number sticker.

It all goes on the same chat, so JD and Georges see the fault with their own eyes when they look at it. The more they have in front of them, the better your case reads.
where is serial number sticker

Usually on the underside of the unit, or on the base of the chassis near the power input. If it isn't there, check the box it came in, the label is often on the end flap.

If you can't find one on either, don't hunt further. Photograph the back of the board instead, any printed code or QR on the PCB works just as well for identifying it.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

That's the one. It reads Model NerdQaxe 12T, Power Input 12V XT60, serial (number hidden).

That's on the chat now, so JD and Georges have the serial with Hal's findings. Send the short plug-in clip when you get a chance and that completes the file.

They're reviewing the return and will come back to you shortly, here or by email.
it won't let me upload video

No problem, the chat takes photos but chokes on video.

A couple of stills do the job: one of the fans spinning with the screen dark, and one of the board with the display module attached. Between those, the serial and Hal's test results, the file is complete.

If you'd still rather send the clip, you can attach it to the email copy of this conversation once we're done here.
can i get it to you some other way

Two easy ways.

Discord is the fastest: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, post the clip in the server and mention JD, he's @nullhashrate there. He's the one reviewing your unit anyway.

Or upload it to Google Drive, Dropbox or YouTube unlisted and paste the link here, that drops straight onto your file.

Either works. And honestly, the stills plus the serial already cover it, so don't lose sleep over the video.
i uploaded it to my youtube chaneel

Paste the link here and I'll put it on your file.

Just make sure it's set to unlisted or public, not private, otherwise it won't open on our side.
https://www.youtube.com/shorts/g4vBCjPnBGE

Got it, that's on the chat now with the serial and Hal's test results, so JD and Georges have the full picture.

That's everything from your side, Todd. They're reviewing the return and will come back to you shortly, here or by email. Nothing to send back until that approval lands.
okay thank you

You're welcome, Todd.

One quick thing while I have you, since it helps us: what made you push that unit to 650 and 1170? Chasing the extra hashrate, or was it running cool enough that it seemed safe?
sorry to be short but i got to leave for work

No problem at all, go.

Everything's on the file and the team's answer comes to your email, so nothing's waiting on you. Have a good shift, Todd.
i added the 120 fans and a side aux fan and temps were never above 50 so i figured i would try it

That's useful, thanks, and it's a fair bit of reasoning: extra cooling in, temps well under control, so the headroom looked real.

I've put that on the file too. Cooling wasn't the weak link at 50C, so it tells JD something about where the fault actually sits.

Go catch your shift. The answer comes to your email.
i'm totally new to all this and still learning

You're running eight units off one RSP-1500 and you diagnosed a board-level fault with us in half an hour. That's not new, Todd.

One thing worth knowing for next time: temps aren't the whole story on an overclock, voltage stress on the regulators matters just as much, and that part doesn't show on the screen.

Discord's a good place for that stuff, plenty of people there tuning the same boards.
ok thank you, i'm still stumbling around  discord, but its getting easier to follow different post

It clicks after a while. Post a question with a photo and people jump on it, that's the quickest way in.

Go get to work, Todd. The team's answer on the NerdOctaxe comes to your email, nothing more needed from you.
thank you again for your time
